claim: Let \(\mathcal F_{10}=(\omega^{mn})_{m,n\in\mathbb Z_{10}}\), where \(\omega=e^{-2\pi i/10}\), and let \(\mathcal F_{10}[\mathcal M,:]\) be the rows indexed by a nonempty proper subset \(\mathcal M\subset\mathbb Z_{10}\). This row-selected harmonic frame is full spark if and only if \(\mathcal M\) is uniformly distributed over the divisors of \(10\) and neither \(\mathcal M\) nor its complement is affinely equivalent, under \(x\mapsto ax+b\) with \(a\in\{1,3,7,9\}\), to \(\{0,1,3,4\}\). Equivalently, among uniformly distributed row sets, exactly the ten affine images of \(\{0,1,3,4\}\) and their ten complements fail full spark.

correctness.rationale: Published necessity and invariance reduce the problem to uniformly distributed affine representatives. The representative census is exhaustive; consecutive representatives are Vandermonde full spark; the {0,1,3} determinant factorization is nonzero for every distinct three-column choice; the {0,1,3,4} orbit has a published exact zero witness; complement symmetry closes sizes above five. The exact verifier independently checks all finite determinants and orbit counts without floating point.

value.rationale: N=10 is the canonical smallest highlighted composite failure of the uniform-distribution sufficiency heuristic. A complete iff classification identifies the exact obstruction orbit and its complement, turning a single counterexample into a sharp finite boundary theorem relevant to harmonic frames and deterministic Fourier sparse-recovery designs.
